51527923.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to CMS sensor chip immobilized MMP-14 catalytic domain (unknown origin) assessed as equilibrium dissociation constant by surface plasmon resonance analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Secondary counte: The catalytic domain of MMP-14 was purchased from Calbiochem, and MMP-14 storage buffer was replaced to PBSP (PBS + 0.05% surfactant P20). Then it was diluted to 25 μg/mL with 10 mM sodium acetate at pH 4.0 and immobilized on a CM5 sensor surface after being first activated by a 1-ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl) carbodiimide hydrochloride (EDC)/N-hydroxy succinimide (NHS) mixture using a Biacore T200 instrument. Ethanolamine blocking was performed next to deactivate the unoccupied surface area of the sensor chip. Flow channels 1 and 3 were used as references. Two compounds, clioquinol and chloroxine, were prepared at a series of increasing concentrations (0.78–25 μM at 2-fold dilution) in PBSP buffer and were applied to all four channels at a 30 μL/min flow rate at 25°C. Sensorgrams were double-referenced with blank channel and zero concentration signals, and the response unit (RU) difference at each concentration was measured during the binding equilibrium phase. The Biacore 8K Insight Evaluation software was used to fit the data to determine K_D values. The RU values and corresponding concentrations were plotted using the single hyperbolic Function (3), where y is the response; y_max is the maximum response, and x is the compound concentration.
original_paragraph.Figure 4 caption: Figure 4. Hit confirmation and validation. (A) Diagram of surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensorgrams. (B) Direct binding affinity (K_D) of two hit compounds, clioquinol and chloroxine. 1:1 Steady-state affinity fitting curves of clioquinol and chloroxine are shown. Determined K_D value of clioquinol and chloroxine was 1.2 ± 0.5 and 2.4 ± 0.9 μM, respectively. Binding level at 10 seconds before injection ended after zero concentration signal subtraction. (C) Cell viability of clioquinol and chloroxine.
original_paragraph.Results - Hit confirmation and validatio: To confirm our main hit compounds using a completely different technique from the enzymatic primary assay, we performed SPR binding analysis to investigate whether clioquinol and chloroxine directly bind to MMP-14. The catalytic domain of MMP-14 (cat-MMP-14) was immobilized on the CM5 sensor surface (Fig. 4A), and a series of increasing concentrations of each compound was injected over the cat-MMP-14 immobilized surface. The determined binding affinities (K_D) were 1.2 ± 0.5 μM and 2.4 ± 0.9 μM for clioquinol and chloroxine, respectively (Fig. 4B).
